questions: Which controller change moved slalom line_loss_events, and by how much? Report the count per run and the off-track count for slalom, s-bend and the oval.
Do slalom line losses cluster at direction changes between opposite bends? If so, does the line_loss mode (last_direction versus a search mode) explain more of the gap than the sensor layout?
Did the oval and s-bend hold their finish rates (20/20 and 20/20 in iteration 9)? If either fell, was the cause the controller or the 0.5 kg mass?

Is there any sign that the 0.5 kg body is jittery under the current gains (steering_oscillation above about 0.35 with low max_error)? If so, I will consider returning to 0.7 kg for the final iteration.
feedback_request.suggested_changes_to_test: Keep the geometry fixed. Test line_loss mode and controller gains on the Integrator's side, not sensor geometry. Do not change wheel_track, span, footprint, sensor y or mass in this iteration unless the controller change clearly fails on all tracks.

intent: Hold the iteration 9 geometry unchanged (best score 669.8) so the Integrator can refine the controller on a stable platform. Geometry values are unchanged: five sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m with y = 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.09 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.5 kg. Success means the oval stays at 20/20 or 16/20 or better and s-bend stays at 15/20 or better, with slalom line-loss falling below 1.9 per run. Any score change should be attributable to the controller alone.
learning: Iteration 9 showed that the controller, not the body, was the main lever once mass was 0.5 kg and wheel_track 0.09 m. Slalom remains the unexplained gap, and every geometry test has left its line-loss near 1.9. Holding geometry keeps the controller result attributable and gives the Integrator a stable platform for the final unseen track.
rationale: Iteration 9 (controller change only, geometry as in iteration 8) scored 669.8, the best so far. The oval finished 20/20 with max_error 0.014 m and oscillation 0.22, and s-bend finished 20/20 with line-loss 0.75. Slalom remains 0/20 with line-loss 1.1 to 1.9 and off-track exits. Each geometry lever has now been tested or ruled out: span (iteration 2, worse), footprint (iteration 3, worse), forward position (iteration 4, helped the oval only), wheel_track (iterations 5 and 6, now at the 0.09 m floor), and mass (iteration 7, helped s-bend, and the 0.5 kg body has since been confirmed with a stronger controller). Body width does not change the off-track limit, which stays at the 0.06 m floor for every allowed width. Speed is not limiting, since the oval finishes in about 1.9 s. The Integrator's written rules (a) and (b) point to holding geometry while the controller is the lever. I considered mass 0.45 kg, but the controller is now tuned to 0.5 kg and the final track is unseen, so a change now would confound the result. I therefore hold every geometry value at the iteration 9 best: wheel_track 0.09 m, sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m in 0.015 m steps with y = 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m and mass 0.5 kg. Expected result: the same platform scores near 670 or better, with any further gain coming from the controller on the sharp and slalom tracks.
